I am estimating FED effort for SFCC-724 "SEO – Indexable Filter Pages with Per-Filter Metadata". I need a precise picture of how the PLP, its filters/refinements, and routing work TODAY. Be very thorough, cite absolute file paths and line numbers.

Investigate and report:

1. **Routing.** Read `overrides/app/routes.tsx` in full. List every route path and the component it maps to. Specifically: what is the PLP route (is it `/category/:categoryId`, `/search`, a catch-all?). Is there any path-based filter route? Is there a `categoryPath` page (`overrides/app/pages/categoryPath/`) — what does it do and what route serves it? Compare against `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx` to see what was changed.

2. **PLP implementation.** Read `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (and any partials in that folder). Report:
   - How are refinements/filters read from the URL — query string (`?refine=...`) or path segments? Quote the actual parsing code.
   - What hook fetches products (`useProductSearch`?) and what params does it build?
   - Is `getProps`/`getTemplateName`/SSR data fetching used (PWA Kit's `Component.getProps`)? Is the PLP server-rendered with data, or client-fetched?
   - What `<Helmet>` / meta tags does it emit today — title, description, canonical, robots? Quote it.
   - Is there any `noindex` logic for filtered views today?

3. **Filter/refinement UI.** Find the refinements components (grep `refine`, `refinement`, `Refinements` across overrides/ and note base equivalents in node_modules). How is a filter click turned into a URL change — `history.push` with searchParams? Quote the handler.

4. **URL helpers.** Read `overrides/app/utils/` (list it) and grep for `searchParams`, `buildUrl`, `getPathWithLocale`, `absoluteUrl`, `url.ts`, `site-utils`, `url-config`. How are URLs built, and how do site/locale prefixes get applied? Check `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js` for the base helpers and note which ones are overridden locally.

5. **Category data.** How are categories fetched (grep `useCategory`, `useCategories`, `categories` in overrides)? Is there a category tree available at build/SSR time that could enumerate filter combinations? Is there anything that lists available refinement values per category?

6. **Prior notes.** Read `.docs/memory/projectState.md` and grep all of `.docs/memory/` for "PLP", "filter", "refinement", "indexable", "SEO". Report anything relevant verbatim with file path. Also grep `.docs/prd/` for PLP/filter/SEO requirements and report the relevant doc + section.

7. **Tests/stories present for PLP** — list any `*.test.*` / `*.stories.*` under `overrides/app/pages/product-list/`.

Return a structured findings report. Do not write any files. Be explicit about what does NOT exist — that matters as much as what does.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. 18	const fallback = <Skeleton height="75vh" width="100%" />;
19	// Base routes deliberately not served. `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` reads this list so the
20	// route registry matches runtime; keep it a literal array of strings.
21	const EXCLUDED_BASE_ROUTES = ['/category/:categoryId'];
22	
23	// Create your pages here and add them to the routes array
24	// Use loadable to split code into smaller js chunks
25	const Home = loadable(() => import('./pages/home'), { fallback });
26	const MyNewRoute = loadable(() => import('./pages/my-new-route'));
27	const ContentfulPreview = loadable(() => import('./pages/contentfulPreview'), { fallback });
28	const CheckoutError = loadable(() => import('./pages/checkout-error'), { fallback });
29	const CheckoutRedirect = loadable(() => import('./pages/checkout-redirect'), { fallback });
30	/*
31	 * Same trap as ProductDetail/ProductList: the base app/routes.jsx loads the confirmation page
32	 * with a relative import that the overrides resolver never redirects. Without this explicit
33	 * entry the Adyen confirmation override is dead code and the base page renders instead.
34	 */
35	const CheckoutConfirmation = loadable(() => import('./pages/confirmation'), { fallback });
36	
37	/*
38	 * The PDP override is reached through this explicit entry, not through the overrides
39	 * resolver. That resolver only redirects imports that *name* `@salesforce/retail-react-app`;
40	 * the base `app/routes.jsx` loads its PDP with a relative `import('./pages/product-detail')`,
41	 * which is never redirected. Without the route below, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail`
42	 * is dead code and the base page renders instead.
43	 */

45	
46	// Same trap as ProductDetail above: the base app/routes.jsx loads PLP with a relative
47	// `import('./pages/product-list')`, which the overrides resolver never redirects. Without the
48	// two routes below, `overrides/app/pages/product-list` is dead code and the base page renders
49	// instead. Base routes.jsx uses this same component for both '/search' and
50	// '/category/:categoryId' — mirrored here as two entries pointing at the one override.
51	const ProductList = loadable(() => import('./pages/product-list'), { fallback });
52	
53	// Hierarchical category URLs (/clothing/dresses/day-dresses, SEO PRD DMU-014): the dispatcher
54	// resolves any unmatched path to a category (PLP), a single-segment Contentful experience page, or
55	// not-found. The base '/category/:categoryId' shape is not served at all — see `..._routes` below.
56	const CategoryPath = loadable(() => import('./pages/categoryPath'), { fallback });
57	
58	// SFCC-84 Recently Viewed Full History page (build plan §B2) — a genuinely new route, not an
59	// override of any base page, so there is no relative-vs-package-path trap like ProductDetail/
60	// ProductList above.
61	const RecentlyViewed = loadable(() => import('./pages/recentlyViewed'), { fallback });

64	  {
65	    path: '/',
66	    component: Home,
67	    exact: true,
68	  },
69	  {
70	    path: '/my-new-route',
71	    component: MyNewRoute,
72	  },
73	  // Must precede `..._routes` — the base array carries its own '/product/:productId'
74	  // entry pointing at the base page, and `configureRoutes` keeps the first match.
75	  {
76	    path: '/product/:productId',
77	    component: ProductDetail,
78	  },
79	  // Same reasoning as ProductDetail above — the base array carries its own '/search' entry
80	  // pointing at the base page, and `configureRoutes` keeps the first match.
81	  {
82	    path: '/search',
83	    component: ProductList,
84	  },
85	  { path: '/checkout/confirmation/:orderNo', component: CheckoutConfirmation, exact: true },
86	  { path: '/checkout/error', component: CheckoutError, exact: true },
87	  { path: '/checkout/redirect', component: CheckoutRedirect, exact: true },
88	  // The base '/category/:categoryId' route is dropped rather than shadowed: category pages live
89	  // at their hierarchical path only, and '/category/...' falls through to CategoryPath's not-found.
90	  ..._routes.filter((route: { path?: string }) => !EXCLUDED_BASE_ROUTES.includes(route.path ?? '')),
91	  // Contentful Live Preview — must be before /:slug so it takes priority.
92	  {
93	    path: '/preview',
94	    component: ContentfulPreview,
95	    exact: true,
96	  },
97	  // No ordering constraint versus `..._routes` above — the base array has no '/recently-viewed'
98	  // entry to shadow. Only requirement: land before the '/:slug' catch-all below.
99	  {
100	    path: RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE,
101	    component: RecentlyViewed,
102	    exact: true,
103	  },
104	  // Category pages and Contentful Studio/Experience pages — fallback after all SFCC routes.
105	  // `configureRoutes` strips PWA Kit's '*' catch-all so this is safely reached only for paths no
106	  // other route matched. CategoryPath renders the Experience page itself for a single-segment path
107	  // that is not a category.
108	  {
109	    path: '/:segments+',
110	    component: CategoryPath,
111	  },
112	];

115	  const config = getConfig();
116	  return configureRoutes(routes, config, {
117	    ignoredRoutes: ['/callback', '*'],

Ongoing product sync via MuleSoft post-migration. **DMU-002 — Confirmed (status flipped from Ready for Sign Off, 2026-06-11).** The PWA-side contract is settled: SFCC displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for product data (JT 04-06), with AP21 as the master of record. Upstream sourcing (the first load draws from **both AP21 and PLM** via MuleSoft, with Magento-enriched data migrated after the initial load) sits **outside the PWA boundary** — the PWA does not enrich or compute product attributes itself, it renders the MuleSoft payload. The earlier RJ challenges (PLM/Magento enrichment) are upstream-of-MuleSoft concerns, not PWA blockers.
12:- Multi-region catalogue assignments and regional merchandising preserved across all storefronts (DMU-003).
13:- Registered customer records (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-25): **only email address and Omneo ID** are migrated to SFCC. Name, phone number, saved delivery addresses, and communication preferences are sourced **live from Omneo at login**, not held in SFCC. The previously requested 20-address cap is no longer relevant (addresses are not stored in SFCC). FE must treat Omneo as the source of customer profile data post-login; degrade gracefully if Omneo is unreachable.
14:- **Customer passwords are not migrated** — customers must reset on first login (DMU-005). See AGENTS.md "Magento password migration" gotcha.
15:- Saved payment card details are **not** migrated; customers re-enter at next purchase (DMU-006).
16:- Historical order records are **not** migrated into SFCC. Order history is accessed via NewStore **through MuleSoft** where customer identifiers match across online and in-store channels (DMU-007, **Confirmed 2026-06-11** — status flipped from Ready for Sign Off). The PWA displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for customer order history (JT 04-06); no order data is held in SFCC. ⚠️ Source-of-truth flag retained: the requirement text + JT name **NewStore via MuleSoft**, while an RJ comment says **"Order history will come from Omneo"** — the upstream source (NewStore vs Omneo behind MuleSoft) is out of the PWA boundary but remains unreconciled; see Open Items. For the ME storefront, only online orders appear in My Account order history; the orders API returns the most recent 50 orders held in NewStore, and until NewStore transitions in ME only online orders are visible — no FE customisation required to filter retail orders (DMU-008, Ready for Sign Off 2026-05-25).
17:- Contentful API connections reconfigured to point at the new platform; no bulk content re-entry needed (DMU-009, **challenged → Open** — RJ: no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful; reconciliation pending). Mechanism note: Contentful integrates as the headless CMS via the **Salesforce App Exchange connector**, consuming content through the Contentful **delivery API** for all customer-facing pages across all storefronts (Third Party Integrations: CMS / Contentful) — i.e. the integration is the App Exchange connector, not a bespoke API rewire.
18:- Product images and digital assets (DMU-010, de-scoped 2026-05-25): **out of scope for migration.** Images and assets are stored and served from Contentful — there is no CDN migration, no asset URL rewrite, and no 301 redirects for asset URLs. The existing Contentful API connection is simply reconfigured to point at the new SFCC platform as part of go-live (covered by DMU-009). (Source note records the **new** platform CDN as **Akamai** (SFCC default), whereas the **current** setup is **Cloudflare** (DMU-020). These are not in conflict — they describe current vs new platform CDN — but the migration must carry existing Cloudflare redirect/SEO rules forward to Akamai; see §2 DMU-019/DMU-020. No asset-migration impact, as assets stay in Contentful.)
19:- Migration approach: initial bulk export + one or more timestamp-based delta migrations + a final delta close to DNS cutover (DMU-011). Migration scripts must be repeatable and capable of multiple delta runs — one-off scripts are not acceptable (DMU-012).
26:## 2. URL Strategy (DMU-013 – DMU-020)
28:- Existing storefront locale prefix conventions preserved (DMU-013) — see [regional.md](regional.md) Section 1.
29:- AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — AU root stays globally crawlable; the bot allowlist in REG-009 exempts search engines and social unfurlers from the human geo-redirect, so `x-default` continues to point at the AU root).
30:- Existing product URL `.html` suffix preserved to maintain indexed URLs and avoid unnecessary 301 overhead (DMU-015).
31:- Category URLs updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`); 301s applied from all legacy category paths (DMU-014).
32:- 301 permanent redirects implemented for all URLs that change as a result of migration — products, categories, content, assets (DMU-017).
33:- All redirects implemented per the redirect mapping document, produced during build phase and validated pre go-live (DMU-018, **Open** — Accenture to propose redirect ownership; Zimmermann IT to review existing CDN rules).
34:- All 301s managed at CDN/edge level to minimise application-layer impact (DMU-019, **Open** — existing CDN redirect and SEO rules must be identified and carried forward, not auto-transferred).
35:- Existing CDN redirect rules and SEO configuration from the current Cloudflare setup preserved and carried forward to the new platform CDN (DMU-020).
39:## 3. SEO (DMU-021 – DMU-041)
41:### Canonicals & hreflang
42:- Canonical tags output on all indexable pages, referencing the preferred URL for the storefront (DMU-021).
43:- Filtered and faceted PLP URLs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP URL to prevent duplicate-content indexation (DMU-022, **Open** — Zimmermann wants the ability to override the canonical on selected indexable filter pages).
44:- hreflang tags applied only on canonical PDP URLs; non-canonical PDP variants do not carry hreflang but **do** retain canonical tags (DMU-023).
45:- hreflang implemented via XML sitemap format, mapping all locale codes to their respective storefront URLs (DMU-024).
46:- hreflang tags consolidated from the current 200+ country-specific tags to ~12 regional/language-level tags (DMU-025) — final structure to be confirmed with the Sparro SEO team prior to implementation.
48:### Sitemaps & robots
49:- XML sitemaps auto-generated per storefront and locale, refreshed daily (DMU-026). Disabled and deleted pages excluded on regeneration (DMU-027). Homepage URLs include trailing slash (DMU-028). URLs blocked in `robots.txt` must not appear in any sitemap (DMU-029).
50:- `robots.txt` permits crawling of indexable pages including the bag page; restricts checkout flow, account pages, search results, and filtered URL parameters (DMU-036).
53:- All product, category, and content pages rendered **server-side (SSR)** for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS (DMU-030).
54:- Title tags per page in the format `[Product Name] [Colour] | Zimmermann` — the legacy "Online" token has been removed as it consumes character space without value. Configurable via BM meta tag rules (DMU-031, updated 2026-05-15).
55:- Unique meta description tags per product and category page, sourced from product and catalogue data in SFCC. Category page metadata remains editable per page and is not auto-applied across all pages (DMU-032, Ready for Sign Off — Zimmermann to clarify what "auto-applied across pages" means before final sign-off).
56:- Single H1 per page template (homepage, PLP, PDP), correct H2–H6 hierarchy, no duplicate heading tags (DMU-033). PDP H1 includes the product colour (DMU-034).
57:- CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level (DMU-035, partial resolution 2026-05-15): **SEO rules and attributes will live in SFCC per storefront** (not Contentful). Still Open: Sparro to define field schema before custom build.
60:- Product and Merchant Listing Schema on all PDPs per Sparro template (DMU-037) — custom build required, not OOTB in SFCC PWA Kit.
61:- CollectionPage, BreadcrumbList, and ItemList Schema on all PLPs per Sparro template (DMU-038) — custom build, Accenture + Sparro to confirm JSON-LD scope and page types.
62:- LocalBusiness Schema on individual boutique location detail pages per Sparro template (DMU-039) — custom build.
63:- Organisation Schema on each regional storefront homepage per Sparro template, with `url` and `contactPoint` fields configured per storefront (DMU-040) — custom build.
64:- Structured data for products includes available sizes and per-offer availability, driven by real-time inventory data (DMU-041).
68:## 4. GEO (DMU-042)
70:The system will deliver the technical foundations required for **post-launch GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) enablement** — SSR, structured data, canonical URLs, and XML sitemaps — ensuring no architectural decisions block future GEO activation (DMU-042). No GEO-specific features are in launch scope.

development. Not a permanent relaxation — tighten back up as the app is hardened. Known
  console errors counted against the current 10: the shopper-context 404 (base SFCC template
  code, not fixable in app code, counts as 2 entries), two base-vendor React warnings
  (`PageDesignerProvider` defaultProps deprecation, a `getServerSnapshot` caching warning), and
  one confirmed real bug — a Suspense hydration "Element type is invalid" error, still under
  investigation (see the Contentful Experience component registration work below).
  **Follow-up (same day):** halving the categories alone didn't unblock deployments —
  `lighthouse:recommended`'s ~30 individual performance/build-quality audits (bf-cache,
  total-byte-weight, unminified-*, uses-rel-preconnect, valid-source-maps, etc.) are each an
  independent `error`-level assertion regardless of category scores, and kept failing SIT Gate
  one at a time across successive runs. All non-accessibility/SEO/security-flavored ones were
  downgraded to `warn` at once (pulled programmatically from the preset's own default options,
  not hand-copied). Every accessibility, SEO, and security best-practices assertion
  (`aria-*`, `color-contrast`, `csp-xss`, `clickjacking-mitigation`, `has-hsts`, etc.) is
  untouched and still fully enforced.
- **GH issue #97** — register custom Experience Builder components (ZimmButton first). A
  Contentful-authored Button's `cfBackgroundColor` is confirmed present in the raw entry data but
  is dropped somewhere inside `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react`'s own stylesheet generation
  (traced deep into SDK internals, ruled out CSP/`defineComponents`/design-token resolution as
  the cause; no fix in the SDK's changelog through the latest version). Registering a custom
  `button` component sidesteps the SDK bug entirely.
- **GH issue #98** — Contentful Preview API token is sent directly to the browser in plain text
  whenever preview mode is active (`useContentful.ts`/`useContentfulClient.ts` are both
  client-side). Delivery token exposure is expected/by-design (Contentful's own model); Preview
  token exposure lets anyone with DevTools open extract a live token and pull draft/unpublished
  content out-of-band. Proposed fix: route Contentful reads through an MRT/SSR proxy, same
  pattern as the existing SFCC OCAPI/SCAPI proxy.
- All integrations need to point to production accounts (SFCC, Contentful)
- Global-e integration (confirm pricing flow mechanism before implementing)
- Didomi consent management (implement per storefront defaults in REG-054)
- Omneo / Emarsys marketing sync
- Adyen payment integration
- MuleSoft middleware connections
- PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout flows
- BOPIS (Collect in Boutique) checkout flow
- Full multi-site routing — 8 SFCC sites across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME). **US site topology updated (REG-005, 2026-07-10):** US splits into two separate SFCC sites — US domestic (`/us/`, SFCC checkout) and US international (`/en-ca/`, Global-e checkout). New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.
- Address autocomplete via Google Maps API
- Narvar EDD + tracking integration
- SEO: hreflang, canonical URLs, sitemaps
- Order-on-behalf (OOBO) for CS agents
- Retail Rewards (AP21) integration
- Gift card PDP, cart, checkout, and GiveX integration
- Promotions engine and multi-currency/FX pricebook setup
- CI workflow split — two complementary workflows, each with a clear role:
  - `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): `unit-tests` (Vitest) + `storybook-test` (Storybook `play` + `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `storybook test --ci`) run in parallel; `e2e-browserstack` on release PRs only. **`storybook-test` job is wired but pending `@storybook/addon-test` and `@storybook/addon-a11y` installation (feature/storybook-v10 upgrade task).**
  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
  - Still open per the Confluence page: exact Test-gate design (deploy-then-gate as proposed, or match SIT's gate-then-deploy exactly) and its scope (P0 suite only, or also bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse).

    const params = queryString.parse(searchParamsStr, PARSE_OPTIONS)

## Structural notes that will drive the estimate

- **The `/:segments+` catch-all is both an opportunity and a hazard.** It already owns every unmatched path, so a filter path like `/clothing/dresses/black` would route to `CategoryPath` today with zero routing changes — but it would be interpreted as category id `clothing-dresses-black`, 404, and (being multi-segment) fall to the noindex 404 branch. Adding filter-path support means adding a resolution tier *between* the category lookup and the 404, and that tier needs to know which segment is a refinement value and for which attribute. `categoryIdFromPathSegments` (url.ts:178) is a naive `segments.join('-')` with no disambiguation.
- **The category/filter representation is already hybrid** (path for 0–1 categories, `cgid` refine for 2+ — index.tsx:693-739). Any new scheme has to interoperate with all seven `navigate()` call sites and both `history.push()` sort paths.
- **hreflang currently strips the query string** (`_app/index.tsx:376`). If filter pages become indexable, every one of them will emit hreflang pointing at the unfiltered base — that has to be fixed in the same change.
- **Sort/limit/pagination hrefs are real crawlable anchors** built by base `buildUrlSet`. Making filters indexable without simultaneously addressing `?sort=` and `?offset=` multiplies the crawl surface across **8 storefronts × 11 locales**.
- **DMU-022 is flagged Open with a Sparro dependency and an explicit "confirm before any canonical work" note** (`projectState.md:191`). The requirement as written ("ability to override the canonical on selected indexable filter pages") implies a *selection mechanism* — which filter pages are indexable — that no PRD currently defines and no SFCC field currently holds (DMU-035, schema undefined).
